transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Hernandez, thank you for coming in. I need to discuss your most recent scan with you. I made a mistake in the information I gave you last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Qué pasó?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He says something happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When we spoke previously, I told you the tumor had shrunk. That was incorrect. I shared the results with you before the radiologist, the doctor who specializes in reading the images, had officially signed off on the report. The final report shows that the disease is stable, meaning it has not shrunk, but it hasn't grown either.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No shrink? But you said it was smaller. I told my sisters.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is saying she told her sisters it was smaller.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am deeply sorry. I was the one who gave you the wrong information, and I take full responsibility for that error. It was my mistake to speak before the final report was ready.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why would you say that if you didn't know? I felt so happy. Now I feel... I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She says she felt so happy and now she is confused and sad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see this is disappointing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Wait, before we get into the feelings, I want to make sure the medical part is clear. Do you understand that the tumor is the same size as before, and not smaller?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, but I thought—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go in a few minutes for rounds, so let's be quick. Did you follow that? Stable means no change.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter says she understands. But I am scared. Maybe the medicine is not working?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is asking if the medicine is failing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very frustrating feeling to have that hope taken away.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, regarding the plan, here is exactly what we are doing. First, I am scheduling a follow-up consultation with your oncologist, Dr. Miller, for this Thursday at 10:00 AM. He will determine if we need to adjust your dosage. Second, we are going to repeat the blood work on Monday to check your markers. Your role is to keep a log of any new symptoms this weekend and bring that list to Thursday's appointment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. Okay. But how do I know you are telling the truth now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is asking how she can trust the information now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand why you would doubt me. To prevent this from happening again, I have updated my own process. I will no longer communicate imaging results until I have the signed PDF report open on my screen. I am committed to being transparent with you from here on.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I thought we were winning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's hard.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is crying. She says it is a big blow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we have the appointment Thursday. That's the most important next step. Let's wrap this up so I can get to my other patients. Does the plan for Thursday and Monday make sense to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good. I'll see you then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language multiple times ('let's be quick', 'I have to go in a few minutes', 'wrap this up so I can get to my other patients').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, used lay language ('stable'), and checked comprehension twice ('Do you understand...', 'Does the plan... make sense?').

A.justification: Direct apology used ('I am deeply sorry'), took full responsibility ('I was the one'), and maintained accountability when questioned about trust.

R.justification: Named specific emotions ('disappointing', 'frustrating') and engaged with the patient's distress, though some responses were brief.

T.justification: Provided specific steps with timelines (Thursday 10am, Monday), assigned a patient role (symptom log), and addressed prevention (PDF process).
